title: lore check: a specs: entry that resolves to nothing gets no finding (report it like broken-relation)
description: Low priority; FILED ONLY, implementation waits for a plan slot. A lore check defect that opum-doc ruled on, relayed by the leader 2026-10-26 and confirmed against lore-cli origin/dev source. The defect, as opum-doc relayed it: "`lore check` reports a `relations:` target that resolves to nothing as the warn-tier `broken-relation` (src/core/check.ts relationFindings, ADR-0021). A `specs:` entry on an Arc that resolves to nothing gets no finding of any tier. bundle.ts keeps it as a dangling graph edge by design, and no rule reads it." A worker showed `lore check` accepting a made-up spec id. opum-doc ruling, verbatim: "the fix belongs in lore, not a per-repository script. `lore check` should report an unresolvable `specs:` entry the same way and at the same tier as `broken-relation`, a warning naming the field, ordinal and target. Prove it both ways: a made-up id warns, and a real spec id does not. Whether `supersedes` and `superseded_by` get the same treatment is lore-cli's call in the same task." The supersedes / superseded_by question is this task's to decide: measure what check does with an unresolvable value in each today, decide, and record the decision and its reason on the task before building.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore check reports a specs: entry on an Arc that resolves to nothing at the same tier as broken-relation (a warning), naming the field, the entry ordinal and the target
Proved both ways in one test: a made-up spec id in specs: produces the warning, and a real spec id in the same field produces none (the real-id case fails if the rule warns on everything)

The supersedes and superseded_by question is decided in this task: today's behaviour for an unresolvable value in each is measured, the decision (same treatment or not) and its reason are recorded on the task, and the decision is implemented and proved both ways
The new finding is documented where broken-relation is (cli-surface and the check rule list), appears in the CHANGELOG, and a mutant removing the new rule fails the test
lore check exits 0 on lore-cli's own docs bundle after the change, or every new warning it raises there is fixed in the same PR
